newsitem.title: USA: World Bank audit says a third of loans fall short.
newsitem.headline: World Bank audit says a third of loans fall short.

text.p: The World Bank said on Friday that an independent audit of some $22 billion of its loans to developing countries found nearly one-third fell short of goals and were deemed unsatisfactory.
The review, conducted by an independent evaluation department at the bank, found that 68 percent of loans had satisfactory outcomes in 1995. That compared to 66 percent in the previous year.
The bank said it was a modest improvement but not a break from the long-term trend.

To be judged satisfactory, a lending project must meet goals that are in keeping with the bank's assistance strategy and must be consistent with the bank's overall goal of poverty reduction. The loans must also use resources efficiently.
The audit reviewed 264 loans to 80 countries.
Looking at factors that affected lending projects in 1995, the bank said war and civil strife played a major role.
It said that the East Asia and Pacific region was the best performing region with 94 percent of projects rated satisfactory.
Africa ranked the lowest, with 49 percent rated satisfactory.
